meta.title: Housing tax credit basis, fee, credit-limit and underwriting rules
meta.review_reason: CHFA adopts a new Qualified Allocation Plan every two years; the 2027-2028 plan replaces S1 for applications from 2027.
meta.scope: Rules the Deal Calculator applies to itemized development costs: grant treatment, the 30% basis boost, the applicable fraction, CHFA's contractor and developer fee limits, CHFA's per-project credit limits, and CHFA's minimum and high debt-coverage thresholds.
meta.methodology: Every value is copied from the statute, regulation or CHFA plan it cites, with a verbatim quote and its location. A rule whose status is adopted and whose source exists is applied. A draft value is shown beside the adopted one and never applied. A rule with no source is shown as rule not sourced and is not applied.

status_values.adopted: In force for the stated period; the calculator applies it.
status_values.draft: Proposed but not adopted; shown separately and not applied.

meta.not_included: CHFA's cost-per-unit and cost-per-square-foot basis limits (published only in the Excel application), the state credit three-test calculation, HUD subsidy layering limits, and CHFA's discretion to award less credit than the calculated amount.

S1.title: CHFA 2025-2026 Qualified Allocation Plan, Second Amendment
S1.version: Adopted by the CHFA Board 2025-09-26; approved by the Governor 2025-11-13

S3.title: 26 CFR 1.42-16, Eligible basis reduced by federal grants

grant_basis_treatment.quote: The eligible basis of a building shall not include any costs financed with the proceeds of a federally funded grant.

also_quote.quote: any portion of the grant is funded with federal funds (whether or not includible in gross income)

federal_grant.note: A grant funded in whole or in part with federal money, including federal money a state or city passes through as a grant (HOME, CDBG, NHTF, Capital Magnet Fund).

federal_loan.note: The statute reduces basis for grants only; federal money lent to the project is a loan, not a grant.

nonfederal_grant.note: A grant with no federal money in it (for example state Proposition 123 or local general funds) is not a federally funded grant.

applicable_fraction.quote: The term "applicable fraction" means the smaller of the unit fraction or the floor space fraction

basis_boost.quote: The Code allows for a 30 percent basis boost for projects located in one of the following areas

sadda.label: HUD Small Area Difficult Development Area

chfa.label: CHFA basis boost (state designation)
chfa.quote: The CHFA basis boost only applies to new construction and rehabilitation eligible basis of federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit projects.

basis_boost.acquisition_quote: The basis boost options above do not apply to acquisition basis.

statute.quote: Any building which is designated by the State housing credit agency as requiring the increase in credit

contractor_fee_limit.quote: Aggregate Builder's Profit, Overhead* as a Percent of Hard Construction Costs
contractor_fee_limit.base: New structures or rehabilitation, onsite work, contingency and accessory structures

developer_fee_limit.quote: Aggregate Developer Fee and Consultant Fee* Limits as a Percent of Certain Project Costs
developer_fee_limit.tested_on: Developer fee plus consultant fee, before any deferral
developer_fee_limit.base_quote: Calculated by subtracting the following costs from the total project costs and applying the allowable percentage rate from the table below

special_population_increase.reason: CHFA must approve the increase; it is prorated by the share of units serving people experiencing homelessness or special populations at or below 30% AMI.

credit_cap_federal_9pct.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for no more than $1,800,000 of the annual federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit for any one project or any one Applicant

credit_cap_state_with_9pct.quote: CHFA will pair, if requested, a fixed amount of $500,000 of standard annual state credit with federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit Applications.

credit_cap_state_with_4pct.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for $10,000 per unit of standard or accelerated annual state credit up to $700,000 maximum per Application

min_debt_coverage.quote: Minimum 1.15 to 1.0 for all amortized debt throughout the initial 15-year pro forma period.

high_coverage_credit_reduction.quote: At the time of application, projects with debt coverage ratios that exceed 1.3 to 1.0 may be eligible for less Housing Tax Credit than the amount calculated
high_coverage_credit_reduction.effect: CHFA may award less credit; the amount is at CHFA's discretion, so the calculator flags it and does not reduce the credit.
